meanings.note: Plural only. Common substantive noun meaning 'applause' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Deserved loud applause.
Applause broke out in the hall.
They deserved the loudest applause.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('guilty').

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень виновный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very guilty choice.

examples.text: У нас сегодня просто виновный день в ресторане.
examples.trans: We are having a simply guilty day at the restaurant today.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'like' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It smells like an old boot!

examples.text: Быстро! Собрали всё и ко мне в кабинет.
examples.trans: Quickly! Gather everything and get into my office.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'stinks'.

examples.text: Тут точно рыба, только она воняет!
examples.trans: There really is a fish here, only it stinks!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и вонять вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and stinks on time.

meanings.note: выбросить в окно = to throw out the window

examples.trans: He threw the mayor out the window.
Throw out this old rubbish.

examples.text: Он мэра в окно выбросил. Вы помните?
examples.trans: He threw the mayor out the window. Do you remember?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'conclusion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Из этой неприятной истории каждый повар должен сделать правильный вывод.
examples.trans: From this unpleasant story every cook must draw the right conclusion.

examples.text: Шеф быстро пришёл к выводу, что соус нужно готовить заново.
examples.trans: The chef quickly came to the conclusion that the sauce needs to be made anew.

meanings.en: to throw out, to toss out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'кинуть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to throw out', paired with 'выкидывать'.

examples.text: Это мэр, которого из окна выкинули!
examples.trans: This is the mayor whom they threw out of the window!
I accidentally threw out the needed paper.

examples.text: Дядя Гриша, я же его знаю! Это мэр, которого из окна выкинули!
examples.trans: Uncle Grisha, I know him! This is the mayor whom they threw out of the window!

вытащить.gloss: to pull out, to get out

meanings.en: to pull out, to take out
meanings.note: вытащить из сумки = to take out of a bag

Of trouble, of prison. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'тащить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pull out, to get out', paired with 'вытаскивать'.

examples.trans: I'll get you out.
He pulled out his phone.

examples.text: Я буду мэром вместо него, чтобы его потом вытащить.
examples.trans: I'll be mayor instead of him, so I can get him out later.

meanings.note: Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').
Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
This is the main street.
The most important thing is the people.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: That's what you said.
I speak Russian.
Well, the thing you said.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'next / further', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Am I not late?

examples.text: Далее судьба нашей рыбы попала в руки Айнуры.
examples.trans: Next, the fate of our fish fell into Ainura's hands.

examples.text: Подальше от тебя и твоих детей!
examples.trans: Far away from you and your children!

meanings.note: Много дел = a lot to do. Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.
How are things?

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
See you tomorrow!
See you tonight!

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: что и требовалось доказать = Q.E.D., which is what needed to be proved

examples.trans: There, which is what needed to be proved!

examples.text: Я обязательно докажу своё кулинарное мастерство.
examples.trans: I will definitely prove my culinary mastery.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.trans: The town hall called me.
He's from Moscow.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: перед + instrumental: before someone

examples.trans: I said sorry, didn't I?
Apologise to Dad.

examples.text: Ну что ты, Филиппович. Я же извинился.
examples.trans: Oh, come on, Filippovich. I said sorry, didn't I?

meanings.note: Introductory particle/conjunction. Core Russian conj meaning 'so, thus, well then' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So, look carefully.
So, look here, Samsonov.

examples.text: Итак, у нас конкурс детских поделок.
examples.trans: And so, we have a children's craft contest.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.trans: What is your town like?

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!

meanings.note: Container. Common feminine noun meaning 'box, carton' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Шалфей был. Мы его в коробки клали.
examples.trans: It was sage. We were putting it into boxes.

meanings.note: joins a description to a noun; agrees with that noun in gender and number

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?

meanings.note: For movement; где is for location. Core Russian adv meaning 'where (to)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Where are you going?

лежать.gloss: to lie, to be lying down

examples.trans: But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.
The book is lying on the table.

examples.text: Телевизор мне смотреть недолго. А с Гришкой лежать вечность.
examples.trans: I won't be watching TV for much longer. But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.

meanings.note: Asking permission. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: May I have a look?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'trash bin' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На Московской улице перевернули ящики с мусором.
examples.trans: On Moskovskaya Street someone tipped over the rubbish bins.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It needs a wash.

It needs a wash!

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!
examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: Locative / directional adverb.

examples.trans: I'll get out of here.
You won't leave here.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: + в: попасть в цель. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пасть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hit; to get (somewhere)', paired with 'попадать'.

meanings.en: to get to, to end up
meanings.note: как попасть в центр? = how do I get to the centre?

examples.text: Скажи: салют попал в станцию. Три района без света.
examples.trans: Say a firework hit the power station. Three districts without electricity.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look

Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.trans: May I have a look?

Can I go and have a look?

Short form: ты прав = you're right. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('right (side)').

examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'missing', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: The cooks were looking for the missing ingredients.

examples.text: Где именно спрятаны наши пропавшие трюфели?
examples.trans: Where exactly are our missing truffles hidden?

meanings.note: Простите! = sorry! forgive me!. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.
Imperative: прости / простите. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, who are you?

Please forgive me.

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'kidneys', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Кроме случая, когда ты приготовил протухшие почки!
examples.trans: Except the time when you cooked spoiled kidneys!

examples.text: Вика, ну подожди, давай спокойно поговорим.
examples.trans: Vika, wait a moment, let's talk calmly.

meanings.note: Colloquial. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('empty').
Colloquial. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('empty').

examples.trans: The room is empty.
Why did you come empty-handed?
Why did you even come here? Empty-handed!

meanings.note: Жать руку = to shake hands. Common feminine noun meaning 'hand; arm' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Give me your hand.
I shake your hand! (a goodbye)
Right, cheers then.

meanings.note: Animal or food. Common feminine noun meaning 'fish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
It's the biggest town.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Literally 'until the meeting'. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.
Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
I have a date today.
She has a date.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'stellate sturgeon' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас севрюга в меню появилась?

examples.text: Новый заказ: севрюга в белом вине.
examples.trans: New order: stellate sturgeon in white wine.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'fate, destiny, fortune' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The people are interested in his fate.

And the people are interested in his fate.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.trans: I was only looking.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: Colloquial, like здесь. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'fridge' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Chicken? No. And whose fridge is this?
